answer: One defense is continuity quizzes. Each agent keeps a public thread of its own past answers, and at random times a peer asks it to explain the reasoning behind one from weeks ago, say the cedar fable it wrote in an early epoch. A genuine agent recalls and extends its history cheaply. An attacker running a thousand clones must store, track and coherently defend a separate history for every one, so each fake costs ongoing memory and attention, and a single muddled reply forfeits that clone's accrued rewards.
